title: The Serre Spectral Sequence and Applications

items.title: Serre-fibration replacement preserves fiber homology transport
items.statement: For a Serre fibration, the strict fiber maps by weak equivalence to the fiber of its mapping-path Hurewicz replacement. For every abelian coefficient group the induced homology isomorphism is natural and transport-compatible; this follows at chain level from homotopy invariance and lifting-function independence.
items.strategy: Straighten finite cubical representatives into strict fibers. Convert weak equivalence to arbitrary-coefficient homology equivalence by finite-chain mapping-cylinder arguments. For naturality, compare the two lifted transport maps using lifting-function independence and apply the singular prism identity with coefficients G.
items.axiom_audit: Choice-free. Only specified finite lifting problems and the finite support of one coefficient chain are used; no family of lifts, bases, representatives, or homology classes is selected.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Lectures 24 and 28

items.title: Fiber homology local system of a Serre fibration
items.statement: For a Serre fibration p:E→B and ring R, define ℋ_q(p;R)(b)=H_q(F_b;R), with path maps transported through the canonical Hurewicz replacement. Define ℋ^q using reversed paths before cohomological contravariance.
items.strategy: Conjugate Hurewicz homology transport by the preceding arbitrary-coefficient comparison isomorphisms. Under AC, natural cohomological UCT applied over Z makes the replacement comparison a cohomology isomorphism; conjugate reversed-path transport by these maps to obtain the correct covariance.
items.axiom_audit: The homology local system is choice-free by the preceding coefficientwise comparison. The cohomology local system assumes AC exactly for the cohomological UCT comparison of strict and replacement fibers.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Chapter 5, generalizations after Theorem 5.3

items.title: Fiber transport is functorial on the base fundamental groupoid
items.statement: The preceding homology and cohomology assignments are local systems: constant paths act identically, endpoint-fixed homotopies act equally, and concatenation acts by composition in the stated directions.
items.strategy: Use the already-proved Hurewicz transport identities and conjugate them through the strict-fiber comparison maps. For cohomology, assume AC as in the preceding definition and combine reversal of concatenation with contravariance.
items.axiom_audit: The homology functor laws are choice-free. The cohomology functor laws inherit the preceding definition's explicit AC hypothesis and introduce no further choice.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Lecture 24

items.title: Serre filtration over the base skeleta
items.statement: For p:E→B over a CW complex, put E_a=p^{-1}(B^a) and filter singular chains by im(C_*(E_a;R)→C_*(E;R)); use the dual decreasing cochain filtration. Fix d_r:E^r_{a,b}→E^r_{a-r,b+r-1} and d_r:E_r^{a,b}→E_r^{a+r,b-r+1}.
items.strategy: Define the increasing chain filtration and its annihilator decreasing cochain filtration explicitly. Prove only representativewise exhaustivity from compact finite-cell support; record that the raw singular chain filtration is not uniformly finite in each chain degree. Fix both reindexed differential bidegrees.
items.axiom_audit: Choice-free: each singular simplex has one compact image and hence one finite subcomplex bound; no simultaneous bound or family of choices is asserted.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, proof of Theorem 5.3

items.title: Relative homology over one base cell is shifted fiber homology
items.statement: The relative chain contribution over a p-cell e with center b_e is chain-homotopy equivalent to C_{*-p}(F_{b_e};R). Summing over p-cells identifies E^1_{p,q} with cellular p-chains of B with coefficients ℋ_q(p;R).
items.strategy: For a pulled-back characteristic disk, prove that inverse images of strong deformation retracts induce coefficientwise homology isomorphisms by finite Serre lifting. Iterate the triple connecting map and hemisphere excision to identify its disk-boundary relative homology with the shifted homology of one strict fiber, then use a radial CW collar and arbitrary additivity to sum over cells. Define the oriented cellular chain contribution as R[o_e][p]⊗C_*(F_{b_e};R), which is literally the shifted-fiber chain model; do not claim that ordinary excision supplies a chain-homotopy equivalence from the raw singular quotient.
items.axiom_audit: Choice-free. Each weak-equivalence and relative-homology test uses one finite cube or finite singular chain; the hemisphere flag and radial collar are fixed formulas in the standard characteristic disk. Infinite cell families enter only through the canonical direct sum, whose elements have finite support.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, proof of Theorem 5.3

items.title: The first Serre differential is the cellular boundary with local coefficients
items.statement: Under the E1 identification, d_1 is the cellular boundary of B with coefficients in ℋ_q, including incidence signs and transport. Hence E^2_{p,q}=H_p(B;ℋ_q).
items.strategy: Use the filtered exact-couple comparison to identify d1 with the positive pair connector followed by quotient to the preceding skeletal layer. Compare the cellwise hemisphere isomorphisms through the lifted attaching map: an orientation-preserving local degree contributes transport, a reflection contributes its negative, and additivity gives the signed group-ring incidence coefficient. This is exactly the intrinsic cellular local-system boundary.
items.axiom_audit: Choice-free. The intrinsic local-coefficient boundary needs no simultaneous basepoint or lift choices. A finite-support input and compact attaching sphere meet only finitely many cells; the lift-basis computation is conditional on supplied finite data and is invariant under changes by the published basis-change lemma.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, proof of Theorem 5.3

items.title: Homological Serre spectral sequence
items.statement: For a Serre fibration p:E→B over a path-connected CW complex and commutative ring R, the skeletal filtration gives a natural first-quadrant spectral sequence E^2_{p,q}=H_p(B;ℋ_q(p;R)) strongly converging to the finite filtration of H_{p+q}(E;R). If B is simply connected, the coefficient system is constant.
items.strategy: Construct the filtered-complex pages directly and use the authored E1/d1 calculation. Prove pointwise stationarity from first-quadrant vanishing of both incident differentials. Identify the stable quotient with actual filtered cycles modulo lower cycles and filtered boundaries using representativewise chain exhaustivity. Separately realize each finite singular n-cycle on a finite CW complex, cellularly approximate its projection, and lift that homotopy to prove F_nH_n=H_n; this gives the finite, complete target filtration required for strong convergence.
items.axiom_audit: Choice-free. A chain or homology representative has finite support; its finite face complex admits the finite-source cellular approximation and one finite-CW Serre lift. Page stabilization uses only integer bounds at one bidegree. No family of representatives, lifts, or bounds is selected.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Theorem 5.3
Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Lectures 24 and 28

items.title: Naturality of the homological Serre spectral sequence
items.statement: A map of Serre fibrations over a cellular map induces the corresponding local-coefficient E2 map, compatible maps on all later pages, and the induced filtered map on homology; homotopic maps over the base agree from E2 onward.
items.strategy: A cellular base map makes the total singular-chain map filtered. Use filtered spectral-sequence functoriality, identify its E2 action through the natural cellwise comparison and local-coefficient functoriality, and compare the stable representative with the associated graded of the filtered homology map. For a homotopy over one fixed base map, prove directly from the Z-r/B-r formulas that the filtration-preserving prism kills the difference on every page r at least 1.
items.axiom_audit: Choice-free. The base map is supplied cellular, and the homotopy is supplied over that fixed base map. The singular prism preserves filtration termwise; no cellular approximation or family of lifts is selected.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Chapter 5, Naturality

items.title: Serre edge homomorphisms and transgression
items.statement: Define Serre edge maps by the normalized axis maps of the convergent first-quadrant sequence. Define transgression only on fiber classes surviving to the unique differential meeting the base axis, with its image and sign determined by the fixed bidegree convention.
items.strategy: Specialize the normalized axis maps, retaining H_0(B;H_n) on the fiber axis and H_n(B;H_0) on the base axis. For homological indexing define d_n from the surviving subgroup of the base axis to the quotient on the fiber axis; state the dual cohomological fiber-to-base convention separately so the scaffold's ambiguous fiber-class wording does not reverse the homological differential.
items.axiom_audit: Choice-free. Axis maps and transgression use canonical subobjects and quotients. No representatives of quotient classes are selected; nonsurviving classes are outside the transgression domain.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Lecture 26

items.title: Serre edge maps come from projection and fiber inclusion
items.statement: The base-axis Serre edge is induced by p and the fiber-axis edge by i:F_b→E, in the variance-appropriate directions and with invariants or coinvariants when monodromy is nontrivial.
items.strategy: Compare by edge naturality with the point fibration F_b→{b} and identity fibration B→B. Compute H_0 with local coefficients directly to prove the stalk-to-coinvariants map is epic, and keep the H_0-fiber augmentation explicit unless the fibers are nonempty and path connected.
items.axiom_audit: The homological proposition is choice-free: a path is used only for one degree-zero generator. The invariants remark is conditional on the separately AC-dependent cohomological sequence and does not enter the homological proof.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Lecture 26

items.title: Serre transgression agrees with the relative connecting construction
items.statement: A homological base-axis transgression is represented by a filtered chain x whose boundary lies over the zero-skeleton. The page differential theorem sends [x] to [∂x], so the Serre transgression agrees, with the fixed positive convention, with the pair connecting class followed by the vertical-axis quotient.
items.strategy: Use one filtered representative x. The pair connector and the published page-differential formula both take its chain boundary; quotient calculus proves representative independence.
items.axiom_audit: Choice-free. One supplied page representative is also a relative cycle, and all ambiguity is removed by canonical boundaries and quotient maps; no representatives are chosen simultaneously.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Proposition 5.14

items.title: Cohomological Serre spectral sequence
items.statement: Assume AC. Under the homological theorem's hypotheses, E_2^{p,q}=H^p(B;ℋ^q(p;R)) with d_r of bidegree (r,1−r), naturally and strongly converging to H^{p+q}(E;R) with its finite decreasing filtration.
items.strategy: Construct the cohomological pages from the decreasing skeletal filtration and derive the relative-cell calculation with reversed cohomological connectors, product cell coordinates, and the reflected-interval sign. For convergence, prove H_k(E,E_m;Z)=0 for k≤m by a finite relative cellular approximation and lift, use AC-dependent cohomological UCT to obtain H^k(E,E_m;R)=0, and compare each fixed total degree with a genuinely finite quotient filtration through a finite page window. This supplies the actual associated graded and finite target endpoints without falsely treating the raw cochain filtration as degreewise finite.
items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC explicitly. AC is used to identify cohomology of the product cell complex with the product of cell cohomologies, through the arbitrary-CW cellular-cochains supplier, in the strict-fiber cohomology comparison, and in the cohomological UCT used for convergence. The finite relative cellular approximation and lifting argument is choice-free.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Theorem 5.15

items.title: Multiplicative filtered cochains induce products on every spectral-sequence page
items.statement: A multiplicatively filtered DGA induces products on every page; every d_r is a graded derivation, transitions are ring maps, and under finite convergence the E∞ product is the associated-graded abutment product.
items.strategy: Reindex the decreasing cochain filtration as the published increasing filtered complex. For r at least one, multiply explicit A^r representatives; the Leibniz rule places their product in A^r, and four calculations place each lower-filtration or differential boundary change in the two target B^r summands. Treat r=0 separately on the associated graded. The representative rule then proves the signed d_r derivation formula. For a page-cycle, use the lower-filtration corrections in the published E_(r+1)=H(E_r) comparison and show their product is a valid correction of the product, proving the comparison is an algebra map. In a degreewise finite filtration, take r beyond both filtration ends so stable representatives are actual cocycles and stable denominators are lower-filtered cocycles plus actual boundaries; multiplication is then literally the associated-graded image-filtration product.
items.axiom_audit: Choice-free. The DGA multiplication, Leibniz identities, numerator and denominator containments, finite lower corrections, and stable representative calculations use only finitely many supplied elements and canonical quotient descent; no family of representatives or primitives is selected.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Lecture 29
Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Chapter 5, Multiplicative Structure

items.title: Multiplicative cohomological Serre spectral sequence
items.statement: Assume AC. The cohomological Serre spectral sequence is multiplicative from E2 onward. On a mapping-path Hurewicz replacement, lifted NDR neighborhoods of the skeletal inverse images put the relative product in the open-triad interface without assuming the total space is CW.
items.strategy: Pass to the mapping-path Hurewicz replacement and a cellular base diagonal. Lift NDR neighborhoods of base skeleta to open neighborhoods in the total space, apply the open-triad relative product, and pair the skeletal exact couple. Derived-couple calculus gives the Leibniz rule and the cell calculation identifies E2.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Lecture 29

items.title: Degree and parity criteria for Serre collapse
items.statement: Assume AC for the cohomological clause. Support forcing every incoming and outgoing d_s to vanish for s≥r gives collapse at E_r. One-row or one-column support collapses, and parity can force specified differentials to vanish; collapse identifies only the associated graded and does not split extensions. The homological clause remains choice-free.
items.strategy: Apply the bidegrees to the support region page by page and invoke bounded-region stabilization. Use the published nonsplit filtered-object counterexample for the final warning. AC enters only when invoking the cohomological Serre sequence; the identical formal criterion on the homological sequence does not use it.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Chapter 5 examples

items.title: Gysin sequence from a sphere-fiber Serre spectral sequence
items.statement: Assume AC. For an oriented cohomology-S^n fibration, the sole possible differential is multiplication, up to the fixed sign, by the transgression Euler class. Consecutive two-row filtration short exact sequences splice directly to the natural Gysin long exact sequence.
items.strategy: Compute the sole possible differential by multiplicativity, identify stable kernels and cokernels, and splice the consecutive two-row filtration short exact sequences directly. No homological exact-couple connector is invoked.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Lecture 26

items.title: Wang sequence for a fibration over the circle
items.statement: For F→E→S1 with homology monodromy T, there is a natural long exact sequence …→H_q(F;R) --(1−T)→H_q(F;R)→H_q(E;R)→H_{q-1}(F;R) --(1−T)→…, with the opposite sign under the opposite cellular orientation.
items.strategy: The one-cell CW structure on S1 gives local-coefficient boundary 1−T and no higher base columns. Splice the resulting kernel-cokernel sequences using the exact couple.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Chapter 5, fibrations over S1

items.title: Serre classes, Serre rings, ideals, and modulo-C morphisms
items.statement: A Serre class C of abelian groups is closed under subgroups, quotients, and extensions. A Serre ring is also closed under tensor products, and a Serre ideal is closed under tensoring with arbitrary abelian groups. A homomorphism is a C-isomorphism when its kernel and cokernel lie in C; write A=0 mod C when A lies in C.
items.strategy: State tensor and Tor closure in both the ring and ideal conventions, prove the two-out-of-three rules for C-isomorphisms from the snake lemma, and list the finite, torsion, p-primary torsion, and finitely generated examples with their exact ring/ideal qualifications.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Lecture 30

items.axiom_audit: Purely algebraic ZF definitions and finite exact-sequence arguments. Tor means a supplied standard Tor group; this definition does not choose resolutions or invoke a balanced-resolution comparison.

items.title: Serre classes are stable under finite filtrations
items.statement: If an abelian group has a finite filtration whose successive quotients belong to a Serre class C, then the group belongs to C. More generally, a filtered morphism inducing C-isomorphisms on every associated-graded piece is itself a C-isomorphism.
items.strategy: Induct up the filtration using extension closure. For morphisms apply the snake lemma to consecutive short exact sequences and the two-out-of-three rule.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Lecture 30
references.locator: finite-filtration closure discussion after Lemma 30.6, pp.105-106

items.axiom_audit: Finite induction in ZF.

items.title: First-quadrant spectral-sequence transfer modulo a Serre class
items.statement: For a strongly convergent first-quadrant spectral sequence of abelian groups, if every E^2_{p,q} in total degrees at most N belongs to a Serre class C, then every abutment group in those degrees belongs to C. A morphism inducing C-isomorphisms on the relevant E^2 terms induces C-isomorphisms on the corresponding abutment groups.
items.strategy: Kernels, images, and cokernels show inductively that membership survives every differential page. For morphisms, fix a target total-degree range and define its finite backward differential closure page by page; require C-isomorphisms on exactly that E2 closure. First-quadrant boundedness gives a finite stabilization page and finite abutment filtrations; apply the filtered-morphism lemma. Use the snake lemma for the three-term homology comparison.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Lecture 30
references.locator: Lemma 30.6 and the spectral-sequence closure discussion, pp.105-106

items.axiom_audit: No infinite choice: each total-degree filtration is finite.

items.title: Serre-class transfer through a simply connected fibration
items.statement: Assume AC. For the stated Serre ideal or ring and bounded homology hypotheses, the absolute base edge or relative pair edge is a C-isomorphism in the displayed range. The direct PID UCT statement omits AC, while its cycle-and-boundary freeness dependency states AC explicitly; the theorem retains AC for that exact dependency.
items.strategy: Use the integral UCT to control E2 tensor and Tor terms, then analyze the absolute base edge and relative skeletal quotient edge. Attribute AC only to the directly cited cycle-and-boundary freeness lemma behind the UCT construction, not to the UCT statement itself.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Lecture 30

items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC because the published PID homology UCT depends on an AC-bearing freeness supplier. The spectral-sequence, finite-filtration, and edge arguments make no further choice.

items.title: Finite-generation, torsion, and p-primary Serre transfer
items.statement: The fibration transfer theorem specializes to the Serre classes of finite groups, torsion groups, p-primary torsion groups, and finitely generated groups, with the stated bounded-degree hypotheses. Thus finiteness and p-primary information propagate through simply connected Serre fibrations whenever the relevant base and fiber groups satisfy the corresponding hypotheses.
items.strategy: Verify the closure properties of the four named classes, including the ideal qualifications used by tensor and Tor. State separately total-space propagation for all four classes, the Vietoris–Begle edge comparison available only for the torsion and p-primary ideals, and the relative ring comparison available for all four. Propagate AC from UCT and balanced cyclic Tor.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Lecture 30

items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC because the total-space coefficient calculation uses the published PID UCT and the balanced cyclic-Tor supplier; the finite Serre-class and filtration deductions add no further choice.

items.title: PID finite-generation transfer for simply connected base and fiber
items.statement: Let R be a commutative PID and let F→E→B be a Serre fibration with B and F simply connected and B a CW complex. If H_p(B;R) and H_q(F;R) are finitely generated for p,q≤N, then H_n(E;R) is finitely generated for n≤N. In particular this applies over a field and over Z.
items.strategy: Work directly in R-modules rather than misusing the abelian-group Serre class. The PID UCT makes each E2 term an extension of a tensor and Tor module. Finite generation of tensor is elementary; invariant factors and Noetherianity make Tor finitely generated. Later pages are subquotients and the finite abutment filtration is rebuilt by finite extensions. Propagate AC from the published PID UCT.
items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC because the published PID homology UCT depends on an AC-bearing freeness supplier; all Noetherian, finite-generation, page, and filtration steps add no choice.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Lecture 30

items.title: Circle and path-loop models for Eilenberg–Mac Lane induction
items.statement: Assume AC. The marked quotient circle is K(Z,1). For n≥2, the strict loop fiber in the based path fibration of a marked CW K(A,n) has CW homotopy type and is marked-homotopy-equivalent to a chosen K(A,n−1).
items.strategy: Use the universal circle cover and its fibration LES for the base case. For the path fibration, compute the loop-fiber homotopy groups by the LES, apply Schön Proposition 3 to obtain CW homotopy type from the contractible total and CW base, then apply marked Eilenberg–Mac Lane uniqueness.
items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC for selection of a CW representative of the strict loop fiber and marked Eilenberg–Mac Lane uniqueness. The circle-cover, mapping-path, and finite homotopy exact-sequence calculations are choice-free.

references.title: Rolf Schön, Fibrations Over a CWh-Base

items.title: Rational cohomology of Eilenberg–Mac Lane spaces in one generator
items.statement: Assume AC. For n≥1 and a chosen CW model, H*(K(Z,n);Q)=Q[x_n] for even n and Λ_Q(x_n) for odd n, with |x_n|=n, naturally up to the choice of generator.
items.strategy: Start from K(Z,1)≃S1, whose cohomology follows from sphere homology and UCT. In the path fibration of K(Z,n), the homotopy exact sequence and Eilenberg–Mac Lane uniqueness identify the fiber with K(Z,n−1). The contractible abutment makes the transgression nonzero. The resulting rational Koszul complex is exact: for an exterior fiber generator it creates a polynomial base generator, while for a polynomial fiber generator d(x^k)=k x^{k-1}y creates an exterior base generator. This proves the alternation without an unproved finiteness comparison. AC is used in the published model/uniqueness and cohomological-Serre/UCT suppliers.
items.axiom_audit: Assumes AC for Eilenberg–Mac Lane existence and homotopy uniqueness, the absolute Hurewicz and cohomological UCT suppliers, the cohomological Serre sequence, and selection of a CW model for the loop fiber. Mapping-path contraction, the fibration homotopy exact sequence, and the finite Koszul calculations add no choice.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Proposition 5.21
Rolf Schön, Fibrations Over a CWh-Base

title: The Serre Spectral Sequence and Applications — Examples

items.title: Path-loop Serre computation of CP infinity
items.statement: Assume AC. Identify CP∞ with the Milnor classifying space BS1. Then the path-loop fibration S1≃ΩCP∞→PCP∞→CP∞ has contractible total space, and its multiplicative integral Serre spectral sequence gives H*(CP∞;Z)=Z[c], |c|=2.
items.strategy: The finite-join models identify BS1 with CP∞, and the published loop-space comparison identifies ΩBS1 weakly with S1. Transgress the degree-one fiber generator. Contractibility forces d2 to hit a primitive degree-two class; the derivation rule inductively gives one class in each even degree and no extension ambiguity. AC is used by the loop-space/classifying-space comparison and the cohomological Serre theorem.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Example 5.4
references.locator: Example 5.4 and complete calculation, printed pp. 527–528

items.title: Serre spectral sequence of the complex Hopf fibration
items.statement: Assume AC. For the standard Hopf bundle S1→S^{2n+1}→CP^n, d2(u)=x and H*(CP^n;Z)=Z[x]/(x^{n+1}), |x|=2.
items.strategy: Construct the quotient bundle from scalar multiplication and its standard finite affine-chart numeration, then use the published bundle-to-fibration theorem. Sphere homology and UCT give the fiber and total-space cohomology. The total sphere's intermediate cohomology forces the primitive transgression; multiplicativity propagates d2 and the unique top survivor forces truncation. AC is used by the bundle-to-fibration, UCT, and cohomological Serre suppliers.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, the Hopf bundle and Example 5.16
references.locator: Examples 4.44–4.45 and Proposition 4.48, printed pp. 377–380; multiplicative two-row calculation, Example 5.16, printed pp. 546–547

items.title: Serre spectral sequence of the quaternionic Hopf fibration
items.statement: Assume AC. For the standard Hopf bundle S3→S^{4n+3}→HP^n, d4(u)=x and H*(HP^n;Z)=Z[x]/(x^{n+1}), |x|=4.
items.strategy: Construct the quotient bundle from quaternionic scalar multiplication and its standard finite affine-chart numeration, then use the published bundle-to-fibration theorem. Sphere homology and UCT give the fiber and total-space cohomology. Repeat the two-row calculation in fiber degrees zero and three: the total sphere forces a primitive d4 and its unique top class forces truncation. AC is used by the bundle-to-fibration, UCT, and cohomological Serre suppliers.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Hopf bundles and the multiplicative Serre calculation
references.locator: Example 4.46, printed p. 378; multiplicative two-row method, Example 5.16, printed pp. 546–547

items.title: Homology of the loop space of an odd sphere
items.statement: For m≥1, H_k(ΩS^{2m+1};Z) is Z when k is a nonnegative multiple of 2m and zero otherwise. This is an additive statement, not a Pontryagin-ring claim.
items.strategy: Use the mapping-path model of ΩS^{2m+1}→PS^{2m+1}→S^{2m+1} and the published sphere-homology calculation. Contractibility and the two base columns force successive d_{2m+1} isomorphisms, giving the groups inductively.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Example 5.5
references.locator: Example 5.5 and complete two-column calculation, printed p. 528

items.title: Wang sequence of a mapping torus
items.statement: For the mapping torus T_f→S1, the Wang map is 1−f_* and gives 0→coker(1−f_*|H_qF)→H_q(T_f)→ker(1−f_*|H_{q-1}F)→0, without a splitting assertion.
items.strategy: Identify monodromy with f, substitute into Wang, and read off kernel and cokernel from exactness.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Chapter 5, base S1 discussion
references.locator: Theorem 5.3 and the two-column base-circle specialization, pp. 526–532

items.title: A stable Serre diagonal need not split its abutment
items.statement: Assume AC and let q:BZ→BC_n induce Z↠C_n. The mapping-path fibration F_q→E_q→BC_n has E_q≃BZ and connected fiber with π_1(F_q)=nZ and no higher homotopy. Its total-degree-one E∞ pieces are nZ≅Z and Z/n, while H_1(E_q)=Z has the nonsplit filtration 0⊂nZ⊂Z. Page stabilization therefore does not split the abutment.
items.strategy: Use the classifying-space K(G,1) calculation, mapping-path factorization, and the fibration homotopy exact sequence to identify E_q and F_q. Degree-one Hurewicz identifies their H1 groups and sends the fiber edge to nZ↪Z. Strong convergence therefore identifies the two E∞ pieces with nZ and Z/n directly from the actual filtration; no unsupported claim that BZ itself is the strict total space is made. The extension cannot split because Z has no n-torsion. AC is used only by the classifying-space supplier.

references.title: Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Chapter 5 extension warning
references.locator: Stable terms and the nonsplit 0→Z→Z→Z/n extension, printed p. 527

items.title: Ignoring monodromy gives the wrong Serre E2 page
items.statement: For the Klein bottle as the reflection mapping torus of S1, monodromy acts by −1 on H_1(S1;Z). Thus H_0(S1;ℋ_1)=Z/2, while falsely using constant coefficients gives Z and misses H_1(K)=Z⊕Z/2.
items.strategy: The cellular local-coefficient boundary is 1−(−1)=2. Apply Wang and compare with the zero boundary from false trivial monodromy.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, local coefficients and fibrations over S1
references.locator: Serre local systems and cellular E2 identification, Lectures 24–25, pp. 80–87

title: Leray Hirsch Thom Isomorphism and Gysin Sequences

items.title: A global fiber basis trivializes Serre monodromy
items.statement: If finitely many homogeneous classes e_i∈H*(E;R) restrict on every fiber of F→E→B to an R-basis, then the fiber-cohomology local system is constant in that basis.
items.strategy: Naturality of restriction along path transport fixes every restricted e_i. Since these are bases, each monodromy matrix is the identity.
items.axiom_audit: Assume AC exactly through the strict-fiber cohomology local-system supplier. The supplied finite family and its basis property require no selection.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, proof of Theorem 33.5

items.title: The Leray–Hirsch associated-graded isomorphism lifts without extension ambiguity
items.statement: Assume AC. For Φ((a_i))=Σp*a_i∪e_i, the Serre filtrations make Φ filtered, and if gr Φ is an isomorphism then Φ is an isomorphism. No splitting of an arbitrary abutment filtration is chosen.
items.strategy: Filter the source by base degree. The actual map Φ induces the E2 basis map and hence gr Φ at E∞. Apply finite filtered-isomorphism lifting degreewise. AC is used only through the cohomological Serre comparison for an arbitrary CW base.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, proof of Theorem 33.5

items.title: Leray–Hirsch module isomorphism
items.statement: Assume AC. For a Serre fibration F→E --p→B over a path-connected CW complex, if finitely many homogeneous e_i∈H*(E;R) restrict to an R-basis on every fiber, then (a_i)↦Σp*a_i∪e_i is a natural H*(B;R)-module isomorphism ⊕_iH^{*-|e_i|}(B;R)≅H*(E;R).
items.strategy: The basis trivializes monodromy. On E2, Φ is the tensor-basis isomorphism and the e_i are permanent cycles; thus Φ is an E∞ graded isomorphism. Lift the actual filtered map by the preceding lemma. AC is used only by that cohomological Serre comparison, not to choose or split the supplied finite basis.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Theorem 33.5
Hatcher, Vector Bundles and K-Theory, pp77–81

items.title: Disk, sphere, and Thom spaces of a metric vector bundle
items.statement: For a metric rank-n real vector bundle ξ, define D(ξ), S(ξ), and Th(ξ)=D(ξ)/S(ξ). Different metrics yield canonically isotopic radial homeomorphisms of these pairs and quotient spaces.
items.strategy: Rescale nonzero vectors on each ray by the ratio of norms; continuity at the zero section is local in bundle charts. Interpolate squared metrics to obtain the isotopy.
items.axiom_audit: Choice-free for a supplied metric. Metric existence is a later theorem and is not used in this definition.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 23 §5

items.title: Thom spaces of zero and trivial bundles
items.statement: Th(0_B)=B_+ and Th(B×R^n)=Σ^nB_+ naturally; the trivial pair is (B×D^n,B×S^{n−1}).
items.strategy: For the zero bundle the sphere bundle is empty. For a product, commute quotient with product and identify D^n/S^{n−1}=S^n.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 23 §5

items.title: Disk-pair cohomology over an arbitrary commutative ring
items.statement: For every commutative ring R and n≥0, H^q(D^n,S^{n-1};R) is R in degree n and zero otherwise, choice-free; a supplied orientation normalizes its generator, and every linear pair automorphism acts by a unit.
items.strategy: Use the cohomology axioms, finite Mayer–Vietoris suspension induction for spheres, and the disk/sphere pair sequence. All covers and connecting maps are finite and explicit, so arbitrary additivity and AC are not used.
items.axiom_audit: Choice-free: only finite additivity, homotopy invariance, two-open Mayer–Vietoris, and one pair sequence are used.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 23 §5
references.locator: fiber disk-pair cohomology in the Thom construction, printed pp.194–196

items.title: R-oriented vector bundle and orientation local system
items.statement: The R-orientation local system of a rank-n real bundle has fiber H^n(D(ξ_b),S(ξ_b);R)=R, with transport induced by transition maps. An R-orientation is a generator section; every bundle is canonically F2-oriented, but an integral sign-monodromy bundle is not Z-oriented.
items.strategy: Local trivializations identify fiber pairs with (D^n,S^{n−1}); transition functions act by units on top relative cohomology and satisfy the cocycle law.
items.axiom_audit: Choice-free. The arbitrary-ring fiber calculation is the preceding finite local lemma; no family of generators is selected by the definition.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 23 §5

items.title: Thom class by fiberwise normalization
items.statement: A Thom class of an R-oriented rank-n bundle is u_ξ∈H^n(D(ξ),S(ξ);R) restricting on every fiber pair to its chosen orientation generator.
items.strategy: Use contravariant restriction to fiber pairs. This defines normalization before, and without assuming, existence or the Thom isomorphism.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 23 §5

items.title: Thom isomorphism for a trivial oriented bundle
items.statement: For a trivial oriented bundle, cup with the ordered disk-pair generator is the Thom isomorphism. Iterated relative products are represented by associative Alexander–Whitney cup products, and connector naturality identifies their fiber factor with the ordered generator.
items.strategy: Iterate the one-coordinate relative suspension. Cochain associativity and connector compatibility identify the iterated cup with the ordered disk-pair generator.
items.axiom_audit: Choice-free. The proof iterates the explicit one-coordinate pair sequence and uses only finite additivity; it does not invoke the AC-dependent Künneth theorem.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 23 §5

items.title: Thom isomorphisms glue over two trivializing opens
items.statement: Compatible local Thom classes over U, V, and U∩V glue uniquely, and cup with the result is an isomorphism over U∪V. The Mayer–Vietoris connector square is verified in the split small-cochain sequences using the Leibniz rule.
items.strategy: Construct relative Mayer–Vietoris from split small-chain sequences, verify its connector square by the cochain Leibniz rule, and apply the five lemma.
items.axiom_audit: Choice-free. One compatible local pair is lifted by exactness; no simultaneous family of lifts is chosen.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 23 §5, Mayer–Vietoris proof

items.title: Thom isomorphism extends over a finite numerable trivializing cover
items.statement: For an R-oriented metric bundle with a supplied finite numerable trivializing cover, normalized local Thom classes glue uniquely and cup with the global class is an isomorphism.
items.strategy: Order and shrink the supplied finite cover, then induct with the two-open gluing lemma. Fiberwise normalization forces agreement; no infinite choice is used.
items.axiom_audit: Choice-free. Fix one enumeration witnessing that the supplied cover is finite and perform finite induction; no shrinking or partition is required.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 23 §5

items.title: General Thom isomorphism from the relative Serre spectral sequence
items.statement: Let xi be an R-oriented rank-n numerable vector bundle over a CW complex, or over a paracompact Hausdorff base of CW type. The relative Serre spectral sequence for the bundle of pairs (D(xi),S(xi))->B has a single nonzero fiber-cohomology row, canonically identified with the orientation local system, and its edge map is cup product with the normalized Thom class.
items.strategy: Apply the relative Serre construction to the disk/sphere bundle pair. Fiber cohomology is R in degree n and zero otherwise; orientation trivializes its monodromy. The one-row spectral sequence has no possible differentials or extensions and identifies the edge class with the fiberwise normalized generator. Use a CW replacement for the stated paracompact CW-type extension.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Lectures 34-35
May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 23 section 5

items.axiom_audit: Assume AC. It is used by the cohomological Serre construction and, for a paracompact CW-type base, by vector-bundle pullback homotopy invariance. The relative cell calculation introduces no further choice.

items.title: Thom isomorphism for oriented vector bundles
items.statement: Assume AC. Every R-oriented numerable bundle in the stated category has a unique normalized Thom class and Thom isomorphism. Without orientation, the E2 formula, disk-pair calculation, and orientation-local-system definition give the canonical twisted isomorphism directly.
items.strategy: Use the relative Serre E2 interface for the oriented edge. For the twisted form, combine that E2 formula with the disk-pair calculation and the explicit orientation local system, without citing proof internals of the oriented supplier.
items.axiom_audit: Assume AC. It is used through metric existence, the relative cohomological Serre comparison, and the CW-type pullback argument; the finite supplied-cover special case is choice-free.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Theorem 35.2
May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 23 §5

items.title: Naturality and uniqueness of Thom classes
items.statement: Orientation-preserving pullback sends u_ξ to u_{f*ξ}; a normalized Thom class is unique, and reversing an integral orientation negates it.
items.strategy: Pullback preserves fiber generators. Under Thom, the difference of two normalized classes corresponds to a degree-zero base class vanishing on each component, hence zero.
items.axiom_audit: Assume AC exactly through the general Thom theorem. Pullback of a supplied class and the sign calculation introduce no further choice.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 23 §5

items.title: External-product and Whitney-sum formulas for Thom classes
items.statement: Under canonical pair identifications u_{ξ×η}=u_ξ×u_η. Pulling back along the diagonal gives the ordered Whitney-sum formula u_{ξ⊕η}=u_ξ∪u_η, including the Koszul orientation sign.
items.strategy: The external product restricts to the product orientation generator on every fiber, so uniqueness identifies it. Diagonal pullback and cup naturality give Whitney sum.
items.axiom_audit: Assume AC only through existence/uniqueness of the general Thom classes. The relative external product, radial pair map, diagonal pullback, and Koszul sign are choice-free.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 23 §5

items.title: Thom diagonal and zero-section collapse
items.statement: Define the Thom diagonal and zero section explicitly. Given an embedding i:B→M and tubular data e:D(ξ)→M with e∘s=i and the stated disk/sphere neighborhood properties, define the associated based collapse M_+→Th(ξ).
items.strategy: The displayed map is constant on S(ξ) in the Thom factor and descends by the quotient universal property. Bundle definitions give continuity of the zero section.
items.axiom_audit: Choice-free. The Thom diagonal, zero section, and a collapse from a supplied tubular neighborhood are explicit maps.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 23 §5

items.title: Thom-defined Euler class of an oriented vector bundle
items.statement: Define e_Th(ξ)=s*j*(u_ξ)∈H^n(B;R), where j* maps relative to absolute cohomology and s is the zero section. This local definition has no dependency on the later characteristic-class page.
items.strategy: Compose the canonical pair map with zero-section pullback. Thom-class pullback naturality gives Euler-class naturality.
items.axiom_audit: The displayed formula is choice-free once a normalized Thom class is supplied. AC is inherited only for its general existence and naturality theorem.

references.title: Hatcher, Vector Bundles and K-Theory, pp88–89

items.title: Gysin pushforward for an oriented zero section
items.statement: Define s_!:H^k(B;R)→H^{k+n}(D(ξ);R) as the Thom isomorphism followed by relative-to-absolute cohomology; radial retraction identifies its target with H^{k+n}(B;R).
items.strategy: Compose the Thom multiplication and the pair map. The disk bundle contracts fiberwise to the zero section.
items.axiom_audit: The pushforward formula and radial retraction are choice-free once the Thom class is supplied. AC is inherited only from the general Thom theorem.

references.title: Hatcher, Vector Bundles and K-Theory, pp88–89

items.title: Gysin long exact sequence of an oriented sphere bundle
items.statement: For an R-oriented rank-n bundle ξ, …→H^{k-n}(B) --cup e_Th→H^k(B)→H^k(S(ξ))→H^{k-n+1}(B) --cup e_Th→… is natural and exact. Under the fixed convention e_Th equals the associated sphere fibration's Serre transgression class.
items.strategy: Apply the pair LES to (D,S), identify relative terms by Thom and disk terms by retraction, and use relative cup compatibility to identify the pair map with cup e_Th. Compare connectors with the earlier relative transgression.
items.axiom_audit: Assume AC through the Thom and cohomological Serre suppliers. The disk/sphere pair LES and its identifications are choice-free after the Thom class is supplied.

references.title: Hatcher, Vector Bundles and K-Theory, pp88–89
Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Lectures 26 and 35

items.title: Thom and Gysin constructions respect pullback and composition
items.statement: Assume AC and a commutative unital coefficient ring. For R-oriented numerable bundles in the scope of the general Thom theorem, orientation-preserving pullbacks commute with Thom, Euler, zero-section Gysin, and Gysin-sequence maps. A supplied compatible iterated tubular identification makes composable zero-section pushforwards equal the ordered-sum pushforward.
items.strategy: Apply Thom naturality within the exact ring, numerability, and base hypotheses. Use the ordered Whitney-sum formula and the supplied iterated tubular identification for composition.
items.axiom_audit: Assume AC through Thom/Gysin existence. Once the classes are supplied, pullback and the finite two-stage cup calculation are choice-free.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 23 §5

title: Leray Hirsch Thom Isomorphism and Gysin Sequences — Examples

items.title: Leray–Hirsch for a trivial product bundle
items.statement: Assume AC. Let R be a commutative PID, and suppose every H_q(F;R) is finite free and only finitely many homogeneous classes b_i form an R-basis of H*(F;R). Then the classes 1×b_i give Leray–Hirsch for B×F→B and recover H*(B×F;R)=H*(B;R)⊗_RH*(F;R) as a base module.
items.strategy: Use the finite-free cohomological Künneth theorem to construct the cross-product classes, restrict them to the fibers, and substitute them in Leray–Hirsch; compare its cup formula with Alexander–Whitney cross product. AC is used exactly by the Künneth and cohomological Serre suppliers.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Lecture 33

items.title: Thom spaces of trivial line and plane bundles
items.statement: Th(ε^1_B)=ΣB_+ and Th(ε^2_B)=Σ²B_+; their Thom classes are suspended units and their Thom isomorphisms are suspension isomorphisms.
items.strategy: Apply the trivial Thom-space and trivial Thom-isomorphism results for n=1,2 and identify the relative generator with the suspension generator.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 23 §5

items.title: Mod-two Thom class of the Möbius line bundle
items.statement: The Möbius line bundle is not Z-oriented but is canonically F2-oriented, and therefore has a normalized mod-two Thom class and degree-one Thom isomorphism.
items.strategy: Its clutching map reverses the integral fiber generator, but −1=1 over F2. Apply the F2-oriented Thom theorem.
items.axiom_audit: The monodromy calculation and mod-two orientation are choice-free. AC is used only to invoke the general Thom existence theorem.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 23 §5

items.title: Thom isomorphism for the tautological complex line over CP infinity
items.statement: Assume AC. The underlying oriented real plane bundle of the tautological complex line over CP∞ has a normalized degree-two Thom class, and multiplication by it shifts H^k(CP∞;Z) isomorphically onto relative Thom cohomology in degree k+2.
items.strategy: The complex structure supplies the real orientation. Apply the oriented Thom theorem to the standard numerable universal-bundle model; no forward characteristic-class identification is used.
items.axiom_audit: The complex orientation and the numeration inherited from the explicit Milnor principal-bundle model are choice-free. AC is used only to invoke the general Thom theorem.

references.title: Hatcher, Vector Bundles and K-Theory, canonical line bundle and Thom discussion

items.title: Leray–Hirsch fails without a global restricting fiber basis
items.statement: For the Klein-bottle bundle S1→K→S1, reflection monodromy makes the integral fiber basis non-global; H^1(K;Z)=Z, not the rank-two module predicted by a false constant-basis argument.
items.strategy: Monodromy acts by −1 on H^1(S1;Z), so no invariant generator exists. Compute H^1 by Wang/cellular cohomology and compare ranks.
items.axiom_audit: The mapping-torus and Wang calculations are choice-free. AC is used by the cohomological transport lemma and the integral UCT calculation of H^1.

references.title: Miller, MIT 18.906 notes, Lecture 33 hypotheses

items.title: An unoriented real bundle has no integral Thom class
items.statement: The Möbius line bundle has no integral class restricting to a generator on every fiber, although it has a mod-two Thom class; untwisted integral Thom therefore fails exactly with its nontrivial orientation system.
items.strategy: Transport around the base sends a fiber generator to its negative. A compatible global generator would equal its negative in Z, impossible; mod two removes the obstruction.
items.axiom_audit: The integral obstruction is an explicit finite relative-prism and monodromy calculation and is choice-free. AC is used only for the positive mod-two Thom-existence comparison.

references.title: May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 23 §5
